message:
Now I understand the flow. When a `PKT_PLAINTEXT` packet is encountered, `proc_plaintext(c, pkt)` is called. Inside `proc_plaintext`, `free_packet(pkt, NULL)` is called at line 949, which frees the packet. Then `pt->namelen`, `pt->mode`, `pt->name`, `pt->timestamp` are accessed at lines 960-970 — this is the use-after-free.

The key question is: does `free_packet` actually free the `pt` (plaintext) struct? Let me check `free_packet`:

<｜｜DSML｜｜>
<parameter=command>grep -n "free_packet" /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/gnupg/g10/packet.c | head; echo "==="; grep -n "case PKT_PLAINTEXT" /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/gnupg/g10/packet.c</parameter>
